description.en: How a steppe confederation reached from China to Hungary in half a century, split into khanates, and how Horde rule over Rus' ended on the Ugra.

text.en: An assembly of Mongol nobles at the headwaters of the Onon proclaimed Temüjin Genghis Khan, supreme ruler of all the Mongols. Within decades the state he created became the largest contiguous land empire in history.

Genghis Khan's Mongols besieged Zhongdu, capital of the Jurchen Jin empire, for more than a year and took it in 1215. The Jin court fled south to Kaifeng, and the city on the site of modern Beijing reportedly burned for over a month.

In 1218 the governor of Otrar massacred a Mongol trade caravan, and Shah Muhammad II of Khwarazm executed Genghis Khan's envoy. The Mongols invaded: in 1219–1221 Otrar, Bukhara, Samarkand, Urgench and Merv fell, and many of their people were slaughtered.

On 31 May 1223 the Mongol generals Jebe and Subutai crushed a combined army of Rus' princes and Cumans. It was the first clash between Rus' and the Mongols; many princes, including Mstislav of Kiev, were killed.
The army of Batu Khan sacked Ryazan, Vladimir and many other cities, and in 1240 Kiev. The Russian principalities fell under the overlordship of the Golden Horde for nearly two and a half centuries.
In December 1240 Batu's army took Kiev after a siege. The last defenders sheltered in the Church of the Tithes, which collapsed.
Back from his European campaign, Batu founded the capital of Sarai on the lower Volga. His realm, later called the Golden Horde, ruled the steppe from the Danube to the Irtysh.

The Mongol army of Hulagu stormed and sacked Baghdad, and the last Abbasid caliph, al-Musta'sim, was executed. The destruction of the caliphal capital and its libraries symbolically ended the Islamic Golden Age.
The Mamluks of Egypt under Qutuz and Baybars defeated a Mongol army in Palestine. The first major Mongol defeat in open battle halted their advance in the Middle East and saved Egypt.

title.en: Kublai Khan founds the Yuan dynasty

text.en: Genghis Khan's grandson Kublai proclaimed the Yuan dynasty, with its capital at Khanbaliq (Dadu), on the site of modern Beijing. In 1279 the Mongols completed the conquest of the Song, bringing all of China under foreign rule for the first time.

Forces of the Russian principalities led by Grand Prince Dmitry of Moscow defeated the army of the Horde warlord Mamai. The victory raised Moscow's standing as the centre for uniting the Russian lands and earned Dmitry the name Donskoy.

title.en: Rise of the Khanate of Kazan

text.en: Khan Ulugh Muhammad, driven out of the Golden Horde, established himself in Kazan in the late 1430s, on the lands of former Volga Bulgaria. The Khanate of Kazan became one of the Horde's successor states and for over a century fought Moscow or depended on it, until Ivan the Terrible took Kazan in 1552.

title.en: Great Stand on the Ugra River

text.en: The armies of Grand Prince Ivan III and Khan Akhmat of the Great Horde faced each other across the Ugra River for weeks until Akhmat withdrew without battle. The event traditionally marks the end of the Tatar yoke over Russia.

source: Steps assembled from the event records included in this atlas.
